clue.text: See one store adopted by reliable person? Not entirely

indicators.note: to be adopted by is to be taken in, so the reliable person holds the other pieces
the reliable person is not given in full, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, good-hearted person
the Roman numeral for one
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: A question about seeing a single shop taken on by a trustworthy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a noun: the diocese a bishop governs. A brick is British slang for a reliable, generous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese over which a bishop presides, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Bitter comments about book or collection of books

indicators.note: the bitter comments go round the outside of the single letter for 'book'

parts.note: bile is bitterness or venomous remarks
b is the standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A critic's sour remarks about a volume, or about a whole library.
explanation.walkthrough: BILE wraps around B. The definition is fair because the scriptures are sixty-odd separate books bound together.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture consists of many individual texts, Genesis to Revelation, gathered into one volume.

clue.text: Be out complaining wildly about latest in restrictive speed control

parts.note: to be out is to be unconscious, asleep

indicators.note: doing something wildly means doing it without order, so 'complaining' plus the added letter is mixed up

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its final one, taken from 'restrictive'

parts.note: its final letter, set 'about' by the jumbled fodder

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling angrily about a strict new traffic-calming scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram supplies more than the second word: its ING ends SLEEPING. A sleeping policeman is the British name for a speed bump, a ridge across the road that forces drivers to slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hump physically limits how fast traffic can go, hence a speed control that restricts drivers.

clue.text: Work with corporation perhaps engaging a Parisienne at the right moment

indicators.note: flags that 'corporation' is only one example of the adjective meaning pot-bellied

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so the corporation word holds the French 'a'

parts.note: a corporation is jocular old slang for a paunch, and someone with one is stout
the French feminine form of 'a'

explanation.surface: A business deal involving a Frenchwoman, closed at just the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a company, but here it is the old joke word for a big belly. 'Parisienne' is feminine, which is why the article is UNE, not UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done opportunely happens at a convenient, well-timed point, which is the adverb's whole meaning.

clue.text: Dissolute youngster mostly covered by spots

indicators.note: a thing covered by another sits under it, so the spots go round the youngster

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
a kid is a youngster; 'mostly' drops the D

explanation.surface: A spotty teenager leading a wild life.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal: a dissolute youngster is exactly the kind of young man once called a rake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a debauched man about town, and the adjective describes that loose, raffish manner of living.

clue.text: Bright red stuff beginning to cover area in pubs

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of 'cover'

parts.note: the first letter of 'cover'

indicators.note: the area abbreviation is placed inside the pair of drinking places

parts.note: two drinking places, an inn and a bar
a is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Red paint or carpet being used to cover a section of the local pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pubs' is plural, so it yields two words rather than one, with the area letter sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a scarlet mercury ore, ground for the pigment vermilion, so it is literally vivid red material.

clue.text: One's always travelling, never off the rails

parts.note: no, as in 'no way', means never
someone off the rails has gone crazy

explanation.surface: A train that is always running yet never derails.
explanation.walkthrough: Travelling and rails push the solver toward trains, but 'off the rails' is simply crazy, and 'never' is the negative that goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer has no fixed home and keeps moving from place to place, forever on the road.

clue.text: Studying figures of miners, nearly all allocated place round track

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: berthed means given a mooring or sleeping place
O is round in shape
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Someone researching the numbers of mining workers, with nearly all given spots around a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' cuts the D from BERTHED, leaving BERTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Number theory is the branch of mathematics that studies integers, so it is a study of figures.

clue.text: Massive sign of drunkenness after moonlit wandering

indicators.note: letters that wander do not stay in their places, so 'moonlit' is rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
the sound of a drunken hiccup

explanation.surface: A huge drunk hiccupping after staggering home under the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in clue order apart from 'after': the drunk's HIC follows the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Monolithic describes something vast and solid, like a single enormous block of stone.

clue.text: Fooled, jilted, not married

indicators.note: 'not' removes the single-letter abbreviation for married from the jilting word

parts.note: a jilted partner has been dumped
m is the abbreviation for married, and it is removed

explanation.surface: A deceived fiancé, left at the altar and never wed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface tells a neat story: being jilted means you did not get married, and it is exactly the letter for 'married' that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be duped is to be tricked or deceived by someone, the same sense as fooled.

clue.text: Harsh, being number one, but missing top spot at Glastonbury?

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the Glastonbury landmark is taken out of the winning word

parts.note: to be number one is to have won
Glastonbury Tor is the famous hill above the Somerset town; a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: A cutting review of a band that failed to headline the Glastonbury festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top spot at Glastonbury' suggests the festival headline slot, but it is the Tor, the hill that towers over the town of Glastonbury in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicious words or treatment are cruel and severe, matching the adjective harsh.

clue.text: Sound producer hard to ignore? Hard to avoid several notes

parts.note: someone vocal speaks out loudly and insistently

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out, so the letter for 'hard' is dropped from the notes

parts.note: a chord is several notes sounded together
h is the pencil grade for hard, removed from the notes

explanation.surface: A musician trying to play a chord that is too difficult, skipping the tricky notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'hard's do different jobs: the first is part of a phrase meaning outspoken, the second is the single letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: The vocal cords are the folds in the larynx whose vibration generates the voice.

clue.text: One off to see Musicians Union over failure, after note's missed

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a concert is musicians performing in union, together

indicators.note: the failure word is taken as it stands after the note has gone from it
the note is missed out, so it is removed from the word for failure

parts.note: a goner is someone or something doomed to fail
N is short for note

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to see the trade union for musicians about a failure once a note has been missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musicians Union' looks like the British trade union but is just a concert. 'missed' takes N out of GONER to give GOER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person attending a performance is someone setting off to see live music.

clue.text: Satisfactory opening in Africa? Very good for African mammal

parts.note: OK means satisfactory

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of 'Africa'

parts.note: first letter of 'Africa'
pi is short for pious, very good in the saintly sense

explanation.surface: A business review saying an African market opportunity looks acceptable, even excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for pious is a crossword staple; 'very good' here means morally virtuous rather than excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a striped forest animal of the Congo, related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Kentucky brought in block for historic NASA mission

indicators.note: a thing brought in is taken inside, so the state abbreviation goes within the block

parts.note: a slab is a flat block
the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: Kentucky supplying a component for a famous space mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is plausible, since American states did build parts for NASA; the state's two-letter postal code is the crossword convention here.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylab was America's first space station, crewed by astronauts in 1973 and 1974.

clue.text: High note to draw out, cut short by piano

indicators.note: the word is shortened, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to bleed is to draw out blood or money
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A high note being held, then cut off early by the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the D from BLEED, and P for piano follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is a short high-pitched electronic sound, a shrill tone.

clue.text: Dancing in mask with new family member

indicators.note: letters that dance move about, so 'in mask' plus the new letter is rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
n is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the family joins a masked ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The masked-ball picture hides a short anagram; 'with' just adds the N to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a male blood relative, someone who belongs to your family.

clue.text: Regarding money, any price is wrong to secure uniform

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the jumbled letters hold the uniform letter
a wrong arrangement is an incorrect one, so 'any price' needs reordering

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An argument that no amount of money justifies buying a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front and the surface stays on its financial theme, so 'any price' looks like part of the meaning rather than fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecuniary is a formal adjective meaning relating to cash or financial matters.

clue.text: English friend welcoming priest travelling in New York

indicators.note: the priest's letters are on the move, so they change places

parts.note: e is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the friend word holds the jumbled priest

parts.note: a mate is a friend
anagram of 'priest'

explanation.surface: An Englishman meets up with a travelling clergyman friend on a trip to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The Empire State Building makes the solver think the answer is a New York landmark, but the definition is the state itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Empire State is the traditional nickname of New York State, found on its licence plates.

clue.text: Crumbling Art Deco villa not right for the good life

indicators.note: a crumbling building falls apart, so the letters of the phrase break up and reassemble
'not' removes the single-letter abbreviation for right from the fodder

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
r is the abbreviation for right, taken out

explanation.surface: A decaying 1930s villa that no longer suits a life of luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: After removing the R, the eleven letters left rearrange into the Italian phrase. The crumbling Riviera villa fits the image of faded glamour.
explanation.definitionFit: La dolce vita is Italian for 'the sweet life', a life of pleasure and luxury, and Fellini's film title.

clue.text: Result is God not being considered

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
an option that is out is not under consideration

explanation.surface: An atheist's conclusion: the outcome is that God no longer comes into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital G makes 'God' look monotheistic, but any god will do and the Greek Pan fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan out is to turn out or end up a certain way, which is what results do.

clue.text: Documentary investigation stage includes brief illuminating moment

indicators.note: the stage word contains the other piece

parts.note: a phase is a stage

indicators.note: the word is shortened, so its final letter goes

parts.note: an aperçu is a flash of insight

explanation.surface: A documentary-making stage that contains a short moment of revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: An aperçu, borrowed from French, is a sudden insight; 'Documentary' is not about film here but about documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is a search through records and paperwork, an investigation of documents.

clue.text: Information provided by corporation blocked by old employee

indicators.note: a blocked passage has something stuck in it, so the old letter sits between information and corporation

parts.note: a fact is a piece of information
a corporation is jocular slang for a paunch, a tum
o is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A former staff member releasing company information.
explanation.walkthrough: As at 3 down, 'corporation' is the belly, not a company. 'Old' belongs to the wordplay rather than to the employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or worker hired to do all kinds of jobs, a general handyman.

clue.text: Ancient creature's small commotion when captured by bloke

indicators.note: a captive is held inside, so the bloke goes round the small commotion

parts.note: a bloke is a man
s is the abbreviation for small
a to-do is a fuss

explanation.surface: A caveman capturing a prehistoric beast that puts up a little struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: A to-do is a British colloquialism for a fuss; the small letter and the fuss go in together as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was an extinct elephant-like prehistoric mammal, so certainly an ancient animal.

clue.text: King knocked out by shock? No electricity in this state

indicators.note: someone knocked out is removed from the contest, so the king's letter leaves the shock word

parts.note: outrage is shocked anger, or a shocking act
R for rex, king, removed

explanation.surface: A monarch floored by an electric shock and a sudden loss of power.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical surface runs straight into the definition, a descriptive phrase for the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a power cut, a period when the supply of current fails.

clue.text: Way of manipulating light, possibly tantalising a lover

indicators.note: 'possibly' offers one of several ways to arrange the letters that follow

parts.note: anagram fodder, 17 letters

explanation.surface: A seducer's trick with the lighting to tease a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: A romantic, candlelit surface hides a seventeen-letter anagram from astrophysics.
explanation.definitionFit: A massive galaxy's gravity bends light from objects behind it, acting like a lens that distorts and magnifies.

clue.text: Peasant uprising caught on old wall-painting

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom up, so the peasant word runs backwards

parts.note: a serf was a medieval peasant
c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
o is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A peasant revolt depicted in an old mural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' is a lovely double: a peasants' revolt in the surface, and a word turned upward in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a mural painted onto fresh wet plaster, the technique of the Sistine Chapel.

clue.text: Troops failing to engage?

definitions.meaning: a unit of soldiers split off from the main army for a separate task
the emotional sense: aloofness, keeping oneself uninvolved

explanation.walkthrough: The military sense of 'engage' (to fight) is the trap: the question mark signals that the second meaning is emotional, not tactical.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a group of soldiers split off from the main force; emotional detachment is aloofness and indifference.

clue.text: Make enquires about cheerful and favoured form of entertainment

indicators.note: the enquiry word goes round the outside of cheerful and favoured

parts.note: to pry is to make nosy enquiries
feeling up means cheerful
a pet project or pet pupil is a favoured one

explanation.surface: A booker asking around about a jolly, popular kind of show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favoured' is the adjective, as in a pet theory, and 'about' tells you the nosy enquiry wraps the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppetry, the art of working marionettes and glove puppets, is a traditional theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: Argumentative type was back, unhappy about interrupting election

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the word for 'was' is read from right to left

parts.note: to have lived is to have been, existed
sad means unhappy

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so 'about' goes inside 'election'

parts.note: an election is a vote
ca is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A contrarian returning, miserable about an election result.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'was' as 'lived' and turning it round gives DEVIL. 'About' is not a container here but the abbreviation CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil's advocate argues the opposite side for the sake of debate, a deliberately contrary figure.

clue.text: Impatiently moved revised clue on probing first draft initially

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so 'clue on' is rearranged
a probe goes inside, so the jumbled clue letters go within the initials
the initial letters are the first ones of 'first' and 'draft'

parts.note: initial letters of 'first' and 'draft'
anagram of 'clue on'

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's editor, annoyed, making them rewrite a clue in the first draft.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter winks at their own trade here, with a clue about a revised clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to storm off with exaggerated, huffy movements, showing irritation.

clue.text: Get better as much medicine's taken? Not initially

indicators.note: the phrase is taken without its initial letter

parts.note: most medicine is taken by mouth; the O is dropped

explanation.surface: A patient recovering because they've swallowed a lot of pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As much medicine's taken' is a whole phrase meaning 'by mouth', and it loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who rallies recovers strength after illness, just as one who gets better does.

clue.text: Pay for one to claim ace held by both sides

indicators.note: a thing held by two hands sits between them, so the ace goes between the side letters

parts.note: say means for example

parts.note: left and right, the two sides
a is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A card player demands a winnings share for holding an ace with both partners.
explanation.walkthrough: The ace sits between L and R, and that unit sits inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is fixed regular pay for a job, so the noun matches the noun pay.

clue.text: Instrument study sure to leave answer to the end

indicators.text: to leave answer to the end
indicators.note: the answer letter departs from its place in 'sure' and is moved to the very end

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

a is the abbreviation for answer, now placed last

clue.text: Spoil fake allotment, though nothing's nicked?

parts.note: a dole is a share handed out; minus O for nothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Allotment' suggests a British vegetable plot but means a share doled out. Cod is British slang for fake.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle a child is to overprotect and pamper them, which is to spoil them.

clue.text: Without compromise, quietly fleeing, being wan with love

indicators.note: the quiet letter runs away, so it is removed

parts.note: pallor is the state of being pale
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
love is nothing, as in a tennis score

explanation.walkthrough: 'fleeing' removes the P from PALLOR to leave ALLOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-or-nothing stance accepts no middle ground, so it involves no concession.

clue.text: Sailor hugging copper after copper is in hospital for a spell

indicators.note: the sailor piece comes after the hospital piece
the second copper sits inside the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: HOSP is a short form of hospital
CU is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the sailor wraps around the copper

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman
CU is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A sailor clinging to a policeman, after another policeman ends up in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Both coppers are the metal, not police officers, and the hospital is its four-letter short form rather than the usual single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hocus-pocus is a conjuror's magic formula, an incantation.

clue.text: Metalworker displaying pirate's legend, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the pirate's legend is said out and respelt

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate of Treasure Island, and a legend is a myth

explanation.surface: A craftsman showing off a tale about a famous buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: The pirate is Long John Silver from Stevenson's Treasure Island; his myth said out loud gives the metalworker.
explanation.definitionFit: A silversmith crafts objects such as cutlery and jewellery from silver, so he is a worker in metal.

clue.text: A city, not on for importing source of macadamia nut

indicators.note: the shortened city takes in the extra letter
the word on is not included, so those letters are removed

parts.note: London is a city
taken as written

indicators.note: a source is a beginning, so the first letter is taken

explanation.definitionFit: An almond is an edible kernel of the tree Prunus dulcis, a kind of nut.

clue.text: Poet's line included in course

indicators.note: something included in another is placed inside it, so line goes within course

parts.note: a path is a course or route
l is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A line of verse studied on a poetry course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'line' a line of poetry, but it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvia Plath was the American writer of Ariel and The Bell Jar, a celebrated twentieth-century versifier.

clue.text: Icy world — Arctic winds — run by wealthy people?

parts.note: anagram of 'Arctic'

clue.text: A horse without covering bolted wildly — only now turn to this?

explanation.surface: A horse without a blanket has run off wildly, so attention turns to the yard only now.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom of shutting the stable door after the horse has bolted: acting too late.

clue.text: Dumbing down Formula One in singular suggestion

clue.text: Funding expert popular, welcomed by hobbyist

clue.text: Animated about strong desire, mostly indirect

clue.text: Below fruit, wee statuette

clue.text: Value penning note in French, describing testing translation?

clue.text: Elegant trimmed fillet presented with character

an air is a manner or character

clue.text: My arrangement for strings and brass instrument

clue.text: Hard stone receiving instant cut

indicators.note: the word is cut short, so its last letter goes

clue.text: Retreats within borders of one European city

parts.note: the outer letters of 'one'
dens are private retreats

clue.text: Trumpet's first sound is false

indicators.note: the first letter of 'Trumpet' is taken

parts.note: first letter of 'Trumpet'
a sound argument is reasonable

explanation.definitionFit: Treasonable conduct betrays one's country; to be false is to be traitorous and disloyal.

clue.text: Special edition's text, rather reduced

explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional issue of a newspaper published outside the usual schedule for breaking news.

clue.text: Officially approve billions? Not so much

explanation.definitionFit: To give something your blessing is to sanction or endorse it formally.

clue.text: Half of them show too little appreciation perhaps for major report

parts.note: the first half of 'them'

explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sound of an explosion, and a thunderclap is a very loud crash of thunder.

clue.text: Satisfactory in a card game

explanation.definitionFit: Poker is the gambling game of bluffing and betting on hands dealt from a pack.

clue.text: Suggestion to leave dodgy bar? Heads off without much analysis

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' removes the first letters of HINT, QUIT and DIVE, giving INT, UIT and IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An intuitive judgement comes from instinct rather than reasoning things through.
